errors.conflict: Someone else changed this provider while you were editing it. The latest version has been loaded; review it and apply your change again.
errors.noAccess: You do not have the platform permission this needs ({permission}). Ask a Super Admin to grant it in Roles.
errors.keyTaken: A provider with this key already exists. Choose another key.
errors.baseUrlRefusedPlain: This address is refused. Use an https address on a public host name.
errors.inUse: Numbers or workspaces still use this provider. Switch them to another provider first (credential mode cannot change while numbers are connected through it).
errors.disabled: The provider must be active for this. Activate it first.
errors.credentialsMissing: The provider has no stored token yet. Add its provider token, save, then activate it.
errors.isDefault: This is the default provider. Make another provider the default, or clear the default, first.
errors.builtin: This is a built-in provider. Its address, version and secrets are edited on Platform settings, WhatsApp.
errors.nothingToDo: Nothing to switch: every connected number of this workspace is already on that provider.
errors.partnerNotConfigured: This provider is missing something its partner program needs: the partner key (provider token), the solution id, or the embedded signup configuration. Check the provider and save.
errors.partnerRefusedPlain: The partner refused this request. Try again, or check the provider settings.
errors.unavailable: This provider is not available. It may be archived or missing a credential.
errors.notFound: This provider or workspace no longer exists. Go back and reload the list.
errors.tooManyNumbers: More than 50 numbers would move at once. Pick a source provider to narrow it, then run the switch again for the rest.
errors.validation: Some values were not accepted. Check the form and try again.
errors.request: The request was refused. Check the values and try again.
errors.unexpected: Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a moment.

secret.placeholderKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored value
secret.willClear: Will be removed when you save
secret.willReplace: Will replace the stored value when you save

bearer.label: Bearer token
bearer.help: Sends Authorization: Bearer with the token of the credential mode.

custom_headers.label: Custom headers
custom_headers.help: Sends the headers you define, with the token, WABA id and phone number id filled in per call.

platform_token.label: Platform token
platform_token.help: One token of the platform at the provider (a partner token). Customers hold none.

channel_token.label: Number token
channel_token.help: Each connected number holds its own access token.

meta_app_level.label: App-level callback
meta_app_level.help: The platform only subscribes the WABA. The callback is set once on the Meta app.

number_level_override.label: Per-number callback
number_level_override.help: After subscribing, the platform sets the callback for each number through the provider.

meta_app_secret_sha256.label: Meta signature (app secret)
meta_app_secret_sha256.help: Deliveries carry X-Hub-Signature-256, checked with the provider app secret.

shared_secret_header.label: Shared secret in a header
shared_secret_header.help: A header you name carries the provider webhook secret itself.

none.label: No signature
none.help: The provider signs nothing. Only the secret in the callback URL authenticates deliveries.

provider_credit_line.label: Provider credit line
provider_credit_line.help: The provider bills the platform from its own credit line.

customer_direct.label: Customer pays Meta directly
customer_direct.help: The customer payment method is on Meta (reseller engine mode meta_direct).

meta_reseller.label: Meta reseller credit line
meta_reseller.help: The platform Meta credit line is shared onto the customer WABA (reseller engine mode reseller).

manual.label: Manual
manual.help: Workspaces paste their WABA and phone number ids.

embedded_signup.label: Embedded signup
embedded_signup.help: Workspaces connect through the Meta embedded signup of the platform Meta app.

gaps.providerToken: The provider token is not stored. Activating this provider needs it.
gaps.appSecret: The app secret is not stored. Every webhook delivery of this provider is refused until it is.
gaps.webhookSecret: The webhook secret is not stored. Every webhook delivery of this provider is refused until it is.

headers.intro: Headers sent with every call to this provider. A header whose value is not known on a call is left out, never sent as a literal placeholder.
headers.name: Header name
headers.leftOut: A header that uses a placeholder with no value on that call is left out. Hop-by-hop and framing headers (host, content-length, transfer-encoding and similar) cannot be set.
headers.channelTokenNeverKnown: This provider uses the platform token, so customers hold no number token: a header that uses the number token placeholder will always be left out.

problems.nameInvalid: Header names use letters, digits and hyphens only.
problems.nameDenied: The header {name} is managed by the connection and cannot be set.
problems.valueTooLong: The value of {name} is longer than {max} characters.
problems.valueCharacters: The value of {name} holds a control or non-ASCII character.
problems.placeholderUnknown: The header {name} uses an unknown placeholder: {names}.
problems.strayBrace: The header {name} has a stray brace. Placeholders are written with double braces around the name.
problems.credentialNotCarried: One header must carry the placeholder {placeholder}, which is how the credential reaches the provider.

placeholders.providerToken: The token of the platform at the provider.
placeholders.channelToken: The access token of the number the call is for.
placeholders.wabaId: The WhatsApp Business Account id of the number.
placeholders.phoneNumberId: The phone number id of the number.

preview.title: Preview of a call
preview.note: Stand-in values are shown. Real tokens and ids are filled in per call and are never shown here.

stepHelp.basics: A stable key, a name operators will recognise and optional notes.
stepHelp.connection: Where the provider answers, and how the platform authenticates to it.
stepHelp.credentials: Whose credential does the work, and the provider token.
stepHelp.webhooks: How the provider delivers inbound messages and proves they are genuine.
stepHelp.billing: Who pays Meta, whether files can be uploaded, and how workspaces onboard.
stepHelp.review: Check everything. Nothing is sent until you create the provider.

hints.key: Lower case letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, 2 to 40 characters, starting with a letter. It cannot be changed later.
hints.baseUrl: https://host or https://host/prefix. The platform only calls public https hosts.
hints.credentialModeLocked: {count, plural, one {# number is} other {# numbers are}} connected through this provider, so the credential mode cannot change. Switch them away first.
hints.providerTokenNeeded: Required before this provider can be activated.
hints.providerTokenOptional: Optional here: each number brings its own token.
hints.appSecret: Checks the X-Hub-Signature-256 of every delivery. Without it every delivery of this provider is refused.
hints.webhookSecret: The value the provider puts in the signature header. Without it every delivery is refused.
hints.signatureHeaderName: Letters, digits and hyphens, for example x-bsp-secret.
hints.verifyToken: Answers the provider subscription challenge. Optional.
hints.billingMode: A label that points at the reseller billing engine. It changes no billing behaviour.
hints.mediaUpload: When off, files go by public link instead of an upload.
hints.onboardingIds: Digits only. These are public ids of the platform Meta app.
hints.partnerPinnacle: Pinnacle gives each number its own key. Store the partner key as the provider token, and the Meta app secret as the app secret (inbound webhooks are verified with it).
hints.partnerSolutionId: Digits only, 5 to 32. The partner solution id from the Pinnacle dashboard.

form.devLoopback: Plain http on a loopback address is accepted only in development, behind a server flag. In production this address is refused.
form.ssrfNote: The address is checked again by the server: https only, a public host name, default port, and every address it resolves to must be public.
form.secretsNote: Secrets are write only. After you save they are shown only as set, with the last four characters.
form.signatureNoneNote: With no signature only the secret in the callback URL authenticates deliveries. Use this only if the provider cannot sign.
form.builtinNotice: This is a built-in provider. Its address, version and secrets live on Platform settings, WhatsApp. Only the name, notes and billing mode can change here.
form.conflictHint: Your edits were not saved. The form shows the latest values.
form.fixProblems: {count, plural, one {# value needs attention.} other {# values need attention.}} Fix the marked fields.
form.created: Created {name}. It starts disabled: test it, then activate it.

review.gapsTitle: Still missing before this provider works
review.startsDisabled: A new provider starts disabled. After creating it, run Test connection and activate it.

problems.labelLength: The name is at most {max} characters.
problems.keyBuiltin: meta and interakt are built-in providers. Choose another key.
problems.keyFormat: Start with a letter, then letters, digits, underscore or hyphen, 2 to 40 characters in all.

baseUrl.length: The address must be between 1 and 200 characters.
baseUrl.characters: The address must not contain spaces or control characters.
baseUrl.invalid: This is not a valid URL.
baseUrl.credentials: The address must not contain a user name or password.
baseUrl.queryOrFragment: The address must not contain a query or fragment.
baseUrl.notHttps: The address must start with https://.
baseUrl.port: Only the default https port is allowed.
baseUrl.host: Use a public host name, not an IP address or a single-label name.
baseUrl.internal: Use a public host name, not an internal one.

problems.headers: {count, plural, one {# header problem.} other {# header problems.}} See the list above.
problems.signatureHeaderRequired: Name the header that carries the secret.
problems.partnerCredentialMode: A partner program gives each number its own token: use the channel token mode.

done.disable: {name} is disabled. Numbers already on it keep sending.
done.default: {name} is now the default for new numbers.
done.clearDefault: The default is cleared. New numbers follow the console WhatsApp setting.

disable.title: Disable {name}?
disable.body: It will no longer be offered for new numbers or assignments. Numbers already on it keep sending, so this is not an outage.
disable.inUse: {count, plural, one {# number is} other {# numbers are}} still on this provider. Switch them away when you are ready.

archive.title: Archive {name}?
archive.body: An archived provider is retired. This is refused while any number or workspace override uses it. You can activate it again later.

default.title: Make {name} the default?
default.body: Workspaces without an override will connect NEW numbers through this provider. Numbers already connected do not move.

clearDefault.title: Clear the default?
clearDefault.body: New numbers will follow the console WhatsApp setting again. Numbers already connected do not move.

test.title: Test connection
test.description: Makes one authenticated read to the provider with its stored credential. Nothing is changed at the provider.
test.pathHint: Starts with a slash. The default is /me.
test.pathInvalid: Start with / and use letters, digits and . _ / - only.
test.idsHint: Only fills header placeholders for this call. It is not stored.
test.channelTokenHint: For providers where each number has its own token. Used for this call only, then cleared from this form.
test.tokenInvalid: At least 8 printable characters, no spaces.
test.forgotten: Ids and tokens typed here are used for one call and forgotten.
test.needManage: You can see the last result. Running a test needs the manage permission.
test.redactedNote: The server replaces every secret with [redacted] before it answers.
test.never: This provider has not been tested yet.

hints.ok: The provider answered an authenticated read. It is safe to activate.
hints.addressRefused: The address was refused (not https, not a public name, or it resolves to a private address). Fix the base URL.
hints.credentialsMissing: The provider has no stored token. Add its provider token and save.
hints.unauthorized: The provider rejected the credential. Check the token and the header names and values.
hints.notFound: The path was not found. Try a read the provider supports, or check the base URL and API version.
hints.rateLimited: The provider is rate limiting. Wait a moment and test again.
hints.providerError: The provider answered with a server error. Try again later.
hints.unreachable: No answer: the host did not respond or the connection failed. Check the address.
hints.other: The provider answered with an unexpected status. See what it said above.

list.title: WhatsApp providers
list.description: Choose which WhatsApp Business Solution Provider the platform sends through, add providers, and move workspaces between them.
list.defaultIs: New numbers connect through {name} unless a workspace has its own override.
list.noDefault: No registry default is set. New numbers follow the console WhatsApp setting.
list.defaultHelp: Changing the default or an override never moves a number that is already connected. Use Switch for that.
list.emptyMessage: Add a provider to route WhatsApp through another BSP. The built-in Meta and Interakt routes always work.
list.noMatchMessage: Nothing matches this status and search. Try another filter or clear the search.

detail.title: WhatsApp provider
detail.gapsTitle: Still missing before this provider works

lifecycle.title: Status and default
lifecycle.description: Activating makes the provider selectable for new numbers and assignments. Disabling never stops numbers already on it.

edit.title: Edit
edit.readOnly: You can view this provider. Changing it needs the manage permission.

overview.title: Overview
overview.workspaces: {count, plural, one {# workspace override} other {# workspace overrides}}
overview.builtinNote: This is a built-in provider. Its address, version and secrets are read live from Platform settings, WhatsApp.
overview.credentialsNote: Secrets are write only. They are never shown again after saving, only whether each is set and its last four characters.
overview.webhookNote: Register your public API address plus this path with the provider. One URL serves every provider and every workspace.

new.title: Add a WhatsApp provider
new.description: Register a Graph-compatible BSP. It starts disabled; test it, then activate it.

assignments.title: Workspace assignments
assignments.description: The provider each workspace connects NEW numbers through. A workspace without an override follows the default.
assignments.noDefault: No registry default. Workspaces without an override follow the console WhatsApp setting.
assignments.existingNote: Existing numbers do not move when you change an override. Use Switch to move them.
assignments.noMatchMessage: Try another search or clear the filter.
assignments.emptyMessage: Workspaces appear here once they exist.

set.title: Override for {name}
set.help: New numbers of this workspace will connect through the provider you pick. Numbers already connected stay where they are.
set.noActive: No provider is active. Activate one first.
set.noteHint: Why this workspace has its own provider. Up to 500 characters.

clearDialog.title: Clear the override for {name}?
clearDialog.body: {name} will follow the default again. Numbers already connected through {provider} do not move.

switch.title: Switch provider
switch.description: Move a workspace connected WhatsApp numbers to another provider. Run a dry run first: it changes and calls nothing.

choose.title: Workspace and target
choose.description: Choose the workspace and the provider its numbers should move to.
choose.targetHint: Only active providers can be a target.
choose.fromHint: Optional. Leave on any provider to move every number not already on the target.
choose.setOverride: Also make it the override of this workspace
choose.setOverrideHint: Numbers the workspace connects later will follow. Applied only when you apply the switch, not on the dry run.
choose.reasonHint: Goes into the audit trail. Up to 500 characters.
choose.targetNotActive: This provider is not active. The switch will be refused until it is activated.
choose.dryRunNote: Dry run: nothing is changed and no provider is called.

workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.narrow: More workspaces exist. Narrow the search.

plan.stale: You changed the choices after the dry run. Run the check again before applying.
plan.title: What would change
plan.description: Tick the numbers to move. A blocked number is not touched.
plan.nothingReady: No number can move yet. Resolve what is listed, then run the check again.
plan.headline: {total, plural, one {# number} other {# numbers}} assessed, {ready} can move to {provider}.

numberToken.label: Number access token needed
numberToken.help: The target uses each number own token and this number holds none. Have the workspace paste one on the number health page, or reconnect it, then run the check again.

providerToken.label: Provider token needed
providerToken.help: The target provider has no partner token stored. Add it on the provider page first.

idsMissing.label: WABA or phone number id missing
idsMissing.help: The connection has no WABA id or phone number id on record. Reconnect it.

reconnect.label: Number is disconnected
reconnect.help: It is only re-pointed, not revived. The workspace must reconnect it before it can send.

numbers.captionPlan: Numbers assessed by the dry run
numbers.willResubscribe: Webhook will be re-subscribed through the new provider first.
numbers.inboundNotWired: The provider did not accept a per-number callback. Set the callback on the provider or Meta app to the platform webhook.

apply.title: Apply the switch
apply.summary: {count, plural, one {# number will} other {# numbers will}} move to {provider}.
apply.understood: I understand this re-points live numbers of the workspace and re-subscribes their webhooks.

confirm.title: Move the numbers?
confirm.body: {count, plural, one {# number of} other {# numbers of}} {workspace} will move to {provider}. Each number is re-subscribed first and only re-pointed when that works.
confirm.rollback: To roll back, switch them back. Message history, message ids and receipts are not affected.

errorHints.nothingToDo: Pick a different target or a different source provider.
errorHints.tooMany: Choose a source provider to narrow the set.
errorHints.disabled: Activate the target provider on its page, then try again.

result.title: Result
result.allMoved: All {count, plural, one {# number is} other {# numbers are}} now on {provider}.
result.noneMoved: No number was moved. See the details below.
result.partial: {moved} of {total} numbers moved. See the details below.
result.overrideSet: {provider} is now the override of this workspace.
result.repointedNote: Disconnected numbers were only re-pointed. The workspace must reconnect them before they can send.
result.inboundNote: {count, plural, one {# number moved but its} other {# numbers moved but their}} per-number callback was not accepted. Set the callback on the provider or Meta app to the platform webhook.

rollback.title: Roll back
rollback.description: Rolling back is switching back. Numbers keep every credential they had, so a number token route needs nothing new; a platform token route needs its token stored.
rollback.unknown: The previous provider of these numbers is not known, so a rollback cannot be prepared from here.

workspaceNote.title: Your WhatsApp provider
workspaceNote.ownToken: Each number uses its own access token.
workspaceNote.platformToken: The platform holds the credential; you connect with ids only.
workspaceNote.mediaNo: File upload is not supported: files are sent by public link.
workspaceNote.none: No provider is available for connecting a new number right now. Contact your platform administrator.
